title: Polarization inhibits the phase transition of Axelrod's model

key_points.claim: Adding a binary (polarizing) cultural feature to Axelrod's cultural dissemination ABM removes the order-disorder phase transition in the thermodynamic limit; it survives only as a finite-size effect.
key_points.evidence_quote: polarization reduces the characteristic phase transition of the original model to a finite-size effect, since at the thermodynamic limit only the ordered phase is present.

key_points.claim: Finite-size scaling on a 2D lattice (k=4, F=10) shows critical diversity q_c grows proportionally to N, so it diverges as N goes to infinity.
key_points.evidence_quote: the finite-size transition point values grow proportionally to the system size as: $q_c(N) \propto N$ .

key_points.claim: The final disordered state depends on the network's site percolation threshold: polarized (two dominant cultures) if it is below 1/2, fragmented multicultural otherwise.
key_points.evidence_quote: a polarized phase is obtained for percolation thresholds below 1/2, a fragmented multicultural one otherwise.

key_points.claim: Simulation evidence: for q>q_c on a square lattice (threshold 0.593) the two largest cultures cover about 10% of the system, whereas on a random regular network (threshold 0.25) they cover about 90%.
key_points.evidence_quote: the two more spread communities include near 90% of the system

key_points.claim: The dynamics has three stages. Cultural uniformization first happens within groups sharing the binary trait, then exchange across binary traits (low q only), then a finite-size-driven convergence to order. The authors read this socially as agents finding empathy through a polarizing feature.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents find empathy on the base of some polarizing feature and then tend to align their cultures.

key_points.claim: The authors extend the single-link mean-field approach to a system of equations for P_{m,s}. It qualitatively reproduces the overlap dynamics, and the stationary active-link density is independent of q and always positive, so no transition appears at infinite size.
key_points.evidence_quote: The corresponding stationary values of $\rho$ are independent of q and always positive, without any discontinuity

key_points.claim: Context: the paper lists the extensions of Axelrod's model in the literature, including complex networks, noise, mass media, mobility/segregation, tolerance, confidence thresholds and dynamic networks. It notes that polarization models with many absorbing states are uncommon.
key_points.evidence_quote: including complex networks [5, 6], clustering [7], social pressure [8], noise [9, 10], external fields [11, 12], dynamic features [13], mobility and segregation [14, 15], tolerance [16], confidence thresholds [17], and dynamic networks [18].

reliability_notes: Full text was available. It is an arXiv preprint dated Feb 2021 and may not be peer-reviewed in this form. It is a statistical-physics study of one abstract cultural-dynamics ABM (Axelrod's model). It covers culture, polarization and network topology, and it does not cover the broader design of artificial societies. Results come from simulations plus mean-field analysis, on small systems (N=1600 in several figures).
